extraction_notes: Datasheet is the KEC Semiconductor 2N5551S technical data sheet (SOT-23, marking ZF), Revision No : 3 dated 2016. 03. 28, 3 pages. The ordering code 2N5551S-RTK/P is the tape-and-reel variant of the 2N5551S die; the datasheet header uses the base name 2N5551S.

Curves were digitized from a 400 dpi raster of page 3 by pixel measurement. Axis calibration was verified against major and minor gridline positions: hFE - IC plot x = 0.01 mA at col 2053 with 186.8 px/decade, y = 1000 at row 618 with 229.0 px/decade; IC - VCE plot x = 0 V at col 529 with 186.2 px/V, y = 0 mA at row 1311 with 4.907 px/mA; VCE(sat) - IC plot x = 0.01 mA at col 2049 with 186.6 px/decade, y = 1 V at row 1950 with 343 px/decade; VBE(sat) - IC plot x = 0.01 mA at col 524 with 186.6 px/decade, y = 10 V at row 1957 with 343 px/decade.

Digitization sample currents (0.012, 0.11, 1.05, 5.2, 10.5, 52 mA, etc.) are slightly offset from round values to avoid sampling on gridline columns; the recorded x values are the true sampled currents.

The hFE - IC figure carries three temperature curves (-25, 25, 125 degC). Only the Ta = 25 degC curve was extracted. Points between roughly 20 mA and 45 mA were omitted because the three temperature curves cross and merge there and cannot be separated reliably at raster resolution.

In the VCE(sat) - IC figure the Ta = 25 degC curve is the lowest of the three at low and mid current (label arrows on the figure confirm this ordering: 125 degC top, -25 degC middle, 25 degC bottom); it dips to about 0.050 V near 5 mA before the steep exit-of-saturation rise above 100 mA. Points above about 120 mA were omitted because the three curves converge into a single near-vertical stroke.
In the VBE(sat) - IC figure the Ta = 25 degC curve is the middle curve (-25 degC above, 125 degC below).

All five IB curves (0.5, 2, 4, 6, 10 mA) of the IC - VCE output characteristics figure were digitized; each drawn curve ends before VCE = 5 V, so the last point of each curve is the last clean column before its drawn endpoint. Runs matching in-plot text labels (IB annotations, Ta=25 C legend) were excluded by continuity checks.

Digitized typical values are consistent with the guaranteed table bounds: hFE 141 at 10 mA sits inside the 80-250 band, hFE 146 at 1 mA >= min 80, hFE 77 at 52 mA >= min 30, VCE(sat) 0.052 V at 10.5 mA <= 0.15 V max, VCE(sat) 0.093 V at 52 mA <= 0.2 V max, VBE(sat) 0.742/0.831 V <= 1.0 V max.

Table limits were recorded with their published source_kind (minimum or maximum) and were not converted into typicals. The hFE(2) row publishes both a minimum (80) and a maximum (250) at IC = 10 mA; both are recorded as separate gain points.
fT is published only as a 100-300 MHz band at VCE = 10 V, IC = 10 mA, f = 100 MHz; the guaranteed minimum is recorded and the band is stated in the conditions. No typical fT exists on this datasheet.
Cibo is specified at VBE = 0.5 V (forward base bias), as printed; this differs from the reverse-bias VEB convention on some other vendors' 2N5551 sheets.

Saturation figure curves are taken at forced beta IC/IB = 10, matching the ratio of both saturation table rows; VCE(sat) and VBE(sat) digitized values at the same IC come from two separate figures under the same stated condition.

Absolute maximum ratings on p. 1 (VCBO 180 V, VCEO 160 V, VEBO 6 V, IC 600 mA, IB 100 mA, PC 350 mW on 99.5% alumina, Tj 150 degC) and the safe operating area figure on p. 3 were examined but only VCEO is representable in this schema; the SOA figure was not digitized because it is an absolute-maximum boundary, not a typical characteristic.
Icbo/Iebo leakage rows, noise figure, and small-signal hfe (50-200 at 1 mA, 10 V, 1 kHz) are outside this schema and were not extracted.
No vendor SPICE model was consulted; all values come from the public datasheet PDF (SHA-256 39406473fae30a16a70d2c80d485bd1d69b6f828cee4e4d4ee9467533449544a).
